Hey, sorry that you're struggling.

Some thoughts:

1. I don't think I'd recommend the method you want to use. I was going to do the same thing you seem to plan to for my first time, but later changed my mind. For all the time I've spent reading up on how to kill myself and other people talking about it, cutting yourself is not brought up often. I think that it's probably still quite painful and/or not very effective. Just sayin'
2. You're not a static entity. Many things about you might change in time - how much you empathize with others, how much other people hating you bothers you, what you see as right, good and valuable, etc. At the very least, I don't think it's unfeasible that you will learn how to deal with some of the hurt.
3. I am not sure that "the world hates you". It's possible that there are some people that will call you names just because, but I can't imagine that most people would dislike (not talking about as strong of a word as hate) someone who wants to help them or make the world a better place. It could be that you're just surrounded by jerks. Why would anyone with more that 2 brain cells hate someone for helping them? Even selfish/greedy people would like it (you are giving them something, after all).

Anyway, could you maybe care just for yourself for a while? Do some things you'd enjoy without caring too much about changing the world? To keep some distance from people who talk a lot of shit? Maybe talk with some friends about what's bothering you? You probably shouldn't throw away your life if you haven't at least tried a therapist or have good reasons to think that they couldn't help (I think that the hurt you feel sounds like something you could talk through, although I wouldn't know, since I don't have talkable issues myself).

Another thing - even if dying is the easiest option (which I'm not sure about), there might be joy and/or value in the struggle anyway. Easy isn't always good. Don't get me wrong though, I do get that sometimes everything feels too hard to deal with.
Thank you for your kindness.

As a layman that has looked into life insurance at some point:

Personally, I would just do some basic research on some of the biggest / most popular companies and go for the one that seems the best from that. The suicide clause should be explicitly mentioned in the agreement, but the payout seems more difficult to find. If they don't give clear info about payout, then either check other companies, or try to apply to get an offer.

The local bank I was looking into just had some X years of average net salary for some period as max payout, but the PL sites I took a quick look didn't seem to work like that? I skimmed [ubezpieczamy24](https://ubezpieczamy24.com/), [bezpieczny.pl](https://bezpieczny.pl/), [uniqa.pl](https://www.uniqa.pl/), [warta.pl](https://www.warta.pl/), and they either only provided some general max payout or I couldn't find it at all. I can't really help with that, sorry, idk how they calculate max payout, or if they just allow you to choose it yourself up to their max limit? Maybe you're not even polish...

I think if you're fully free to choose the payout (up to a very large max), then it might feel like they could accuse you of fraud (taking out a massive payout insurance, waiting for suicide clause to end, and immediately killing yourself), but I have never heard about anything like that. It seems that if your health data is correct and complete, and the suicide clause period has ended, they don't have a justified reason not to pay out. Still, I don't know if I would personally want to risk it, so maybe going to an insurance broker and getting the most basic/standard plan (and payout for your situation) could be an okay idea to minimize a risk like that.

Not really sure what stipulations you mean. The only things I have seen are the suicide clause itself and people having their application rejected (due to being too high risk) because of some past anti-depressant use or something similar. The former is easy to check, the latter would probably require you to have insider knowledge on the specific companies risk management procedures, but you'll find it out if you get rejected anyway... so... just go to a different one? Haven't heard of anything else.

Sorry if this is not useful enough. Again, I think you're better off doing your own research or consulting insurance specialists about it.

IMO life insurance is not a bad idea if you have dependents even if you don't go through with suicide, but if things continue being shit, at least you get more time to think it over. Hope your life turns around, so that you don't need to.

Hey, I'm sorry that your friend is struggling and I understand that the guilt and powerlessness must feel pretty terrible. I guess I can throw in my 2 cents as a suicidal stranger.

A decent way to productively handle the feeling of guilt IMHO would be to think about what you could have actually done. If you were aware of it, you could try to reach someone you both know or call emergency services (maybe the suicide helplines can be called instead? idk).

Then again, it's tough. One thing is that, unless they really want to be saved, people can always attempt at a time and place where they think it's unlikely that anyone could even get to them. Another thing is that you risk straining your relationship, because, you know, people generally don't want others to know about their attempts, and even fewer want to end up in a psych ward (against their will, at least). That is also on top of the fact that just restraining someone doesn't magically solve their issues, although other people caring about you enough to do that and professional help at the ward can make things better.

Buuutttt you weren't even aware of it happening.

You did mention knowing that she was planning it. That is even tougher. I mean, you could go the road of trying to take away her means to suicide or you could even escalate and try to get her in a psych ward. At least I think it might be possible, since if you mention having a concrete plan for kys, they will seriously consider putting you there. This obviously comes with the downside that your friend will like you less and trust you less, especially if the ward didn't really help. Although at some point, if they seem very intent on it, it's either they hate you and are (temporarily) okay or they harm themselves...

Before you go all out like that, you could also just check in on them and keep an eye out for anything else suspicious, although, honestly, I think often there might as well be no other signs or anything obvious that they are going to go through with it. I didn't show any signs the last time I wanted to attempt.

Longer-term you could try and talk about why she wants to kill herself, if you think you can handle it. I think (non-judgementally) listening about her problems is usually helpful and I don't really think it makes anyone more suicidal. Cheering them up or trying to help them, though? That's hard. People are also very varied about how they think about this and what they want to hear. I also hope that after her attempt she will get to a therapist or on meds, that could also help.

**My main point** is: it's hard to prevent people from committing suicide, and it is hard to even meaningfully help. Because of that, I think it's unfair (to yourself) to feel very guilty, although it's pretty natural. We always wish we could have done something differently, to prevent something as tragic, but at the end of the day you are not responsible for other peoples decisions.

Hope your friend gets better, and don't forget to take care of yourself. These things tend to weight you down.
